rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensified form means the king wanted Joseph exclusively for himself, implying close attachment and work together.
rows.anchor: السين والتاء في { أستخلصه } للمبالغة ، مثلها في استجاب واستأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king recognized Joseph’s fitness through wisdom, knowledge, endurance, good character, and integrity, all warranting his selection.
rows.anchor: وقد دل الملك على استحقاق يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative omits that Joseph was brought before the king; the clause presupposes this event.
rows.anchor: أي بيوسف عليه السلام فحضر لديه وكلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object pronoun in “he spoke to him” refers to the king; Joseph speaks, impressing him with wisdom and manners.
rows.anchor: فالمكلم هو يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king’s response indicates admiration for Joseph’s eloquence and judgment, making him worthy of trust and nearness.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى حسن منطقه وبلاغة قوله وأصالة رأيه رآه أهلا لثقته وتقريبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makīn describes someone of great rank, derived from becoming established in a place.
rows.anchor: صفة مشبهة من مكن بضم الكاف إذا صار ذا مكانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amīn is a passive intensive form: someone trusted to safeguard what is entrusted to him.
rows.anchor: أي موثوق به في حفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointment formula gathers the ruler’s needed traits: rank entails knowledge and power, while trust entails wisdom and justice.
rows.anchor: وهذه صيغة تولية جامعة لكل ما يحتاج إليه ولي الأمر من الخصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise hints that the king will rely on Joseph in governing and seek his counsel, prompting Joseph’s request to manage the treasuries.
rows.anchor: وهذا التنويه بشأنه والثناء عليه تعريض بأنه يريد الاستعانة به في أمور مملكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s request is presented as his reply to the king, with a separate clause marking dialogue.
rows.anchor: حكاية جوابه لكلام الملك ولذلك فصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition “over” metaphorically means control and authority over the treasuries.
rows.anchor: و { على } هنا للاستعلاء المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treasuries were existing royal funds in Egypt, not later stores created to preserve food for famine years.
rows.anchor: المراد من { خزائن الأرض } خزائن كانت موجودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph sought public service, fair preservation and distribution of state funds, and care for the people rather than personal wealth.
rows.anchor: ولكنه سأل أن يوليه خزائن المملكة ليحفظ الأموال ويعدل في توزيعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains his request by two rare capacities: preserving what is entrusted and knowing how to administer it, thus meriting the king’s trust.
rows.anchor: وهما : الحفظ لما يليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s public declaration of his merit is a form of hisba that guides people to follow his example.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا تعريف بفضله ليهتدي الناس إلى اتباعه وهذا من قبيل الحسبة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya compares Joseph’s situation with Abū Bakr accepting the caliphate despite an Anṣārī adviser urging him not to rule even two people.
rows.anchor: وشبه ابن عطية بمقام يوسف عليه السلام هذا مقام أبي بكر رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s comparison apt because both Joseph and Abū Bakr were ṣiddīq.
rows.anchor: قلت : وهو تشبيه رشيق ، إذ كلاهما صديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qualified person should offer himself for public office when he knows no one else is suitable, as sincere counsel for the community.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية أصل لوجوب عرض المرء نفسه لولاية عمل من أمور الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This especially applies when the candidate is not suspected of preferring personal gain over public welfare.
rows.anchor: وخاصة إذا لم يكن ممن يتهم على إيثار منفعة نفسه على مصلحة الأمة

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سمرة
rows.claim: The Prophet warned ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Samura not to request authority, since requested office leaves one unaided while unsolicited appointment brings aid.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن سمرة قال : قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith does not conflict with Joseph’s request: Ibn Samura was neither uniquely virtuous nor superior to all peers, unlike Joseph in Egypt.
rows.anchor: لأن عبد الرحمن بن سمرة لم يكن منفردا بالفضل من بين أمثاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabawwuʾ means settling or residing in a place, from taking a place to return to; compare Moses’ instruction in Egypt.
rows.anchor: والتبوؤ : اتخاذ مكان للبوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s ability to settle wherever he wished is a metaphor for control throughout Egypt; the clause may be circumstantial or explanatory.
rows.anchor: كناية عن تصرفه في جميع مملكة مصر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read “where he wishes” with a third-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { حيث يشاء } بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads “where We will,” with the divine plural meaning where God wills, commands, or inspires.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير { حيث نشاء } بنون العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two readings convey the same meaning because Joseph wills only what God has willed.
rows.anchor: والمعنى متحد لأنه لا يشاء إلا ما شاءه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement generalizes God’s mercy and reward: Joseph’s worldly gifts reward his excellence, while the afterlife reward is better for him and all believers who are mindful.
rows.anchor: لأن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith appears as a completed past act because it is a settled conviction; piety is ongoing because commands and actions recur across time.
rows.anchor: لأن الإيمان عقد القلب الجازم فهو حاصل دفعة واحدة وأما التقوى فهي متجددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative omits the end of the minister’s wife’s affair and the years of abundance and famine because they do not serve the surah’s aim of showing prophets’ adversity and eventual vindication.
rows.anchor: طوى القرآن أخرة أمر امرأة العزيز وحلول سني الخصب والادخار ثم اعتراء سني القحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story turns to Joseph’s brothers needing his favor, reunion with his beloved brother and parents, and his forgiveness and kinship, which display his virtues.
rows.anchor: لأن لذلك كله أثرا في معرفة فضائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers came from Palestine to obtain provisions in the second famine year; Benjamin remained because he was young.
rows.anchor: وكان مجيئهم في السنة الثانية من سني القحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All ten brothers likely travelled because rationing followed the number of recipients and travelling together deterred highway robbers.
rows.anchor: لعل ذلك لأن التزويد من الطعام كان بتقدير يراعى فيه عدد الممتارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their purpose as provision-seekers follows from Joseph’s appointment over Egypt’s treasuries and his statement that he gives full measure.
rows.anchor: وقد عرف أنهم جاءوا ممتارين من تقدم قوله : { قال اجعلني على خزائن الأرض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph personally supervised food sales because preventing waste mattered to the nation’s survival.
rows.anchor: ودخولهم عليه يدل على أنه كان يراقب أمر بيع الطعام بحضوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph recognized his brothers after many years through strong insight and intelligence.
rows.anchor: عرف يوسف عليه السلام إخوته بعد مضي سنين على فراقهم لقوة فراسته وزكانة عقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their nonrecognition is expressed as a stable nominal state, while his recognition is a verbal event arising when he saw them.
rows.anchor: ووقع الإخبار عنهم بالجملة الإسمية للدلالة على أن عدم معرفتهم به أمر ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reinforcing lām in “they do not recognize him” emphasizes how completely they failed to know Joseph.
rows.anchor: وقرن مفعول { منكرون } الذي هو ضمير يوسف عليه السلام بلام التقوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting “to him” serves the cadence and emphasizes their failure to recognize Joseph, which God caused despite his recognizable features.
rows.anchor: للاهتمام بتعلق نكرتهم إياه للتنبيه على أن ذلك من صنع الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihāz means what a traveller needs, especially the load for the journey; tajhīz means supplying those provisions.
rows.anchor: والجهاز بفتح الجيم وكسرها ما يحتاج إليه المسافر

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah’s account says Joseph posed as if suspecting the brothers of espionage; they described their father and family, allowing him to demand their younger brother as a hostage.
rows.anchor: وفي التوراة أن يوسف عليه السلام احتال لذلك بأن أوهمهم أنه اتهمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A brother of yours from your father” means a paternal half-brother, not a full brother, by implication of restricting the relation to their father.
rows.anchor: و { من أبيكم } حال من ( أخ لكم ) أي أخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph uses an indefinite “a brother of yours” instead of “your brother” to pretend that he does not know them or the sibling they mentioned.
rows.anchor: فعدل عن الإضافة المقتضية المعرفة إلى التنكير تنابها في التظاهر بجهله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not come near me again” means they must not return to Egypt without their brother; Joseph knew they would not leave him behind as a hostage.
rows.anchor: { ولا تقربون } أي لا تعودوا إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of full measure and good hospitality entices them to return; their initial ration cannot feed a large household.
rows.anchor: ترغيب لهم في العود إليه ؛ وقد علم أنهم مضطرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling himself the best host indicates that Joseph lodged the many visitors coming to Egypt for provisions.
rows.anchor: ودل قوله : خير المنزلين } على أنه كان ينزل الممتارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement promises full measure and generous lodging if they bring their brother.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة كناية عن الوعد بأن يوفي لهم الكيل ويكرم ضيافتهم إن أتوا بأخيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No measure for you with me” uses the verbal noun for measuring: they will not be measured grain, a metonym for refusing to sell them food.
rows.anchor: فمعنى { فلا كيل لكم عندي } أي لا يكال لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to exert their utmost effort, while their wording signals that persuading their father will be difficult; “we will try to prevail upon him.”
rows.anchor: وعد بأن يبذلوا قصارى جهدهم في الإتيان بأخيهم وإشعار بصعوبة ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their assurance is attached to the promise and strengthened by a nominal clause and emphatic particle.
rows.anchor: وأكدوا ذلك بالجملة الإسمية وحرف التأكيد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read “his young servants” with the broken plural fitiyah, like akh/ikhwah.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور { لفتيته } بوزن فعلة جمع تكسير

rows.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، حفص عن عاصم، وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and Khalaf read fitiyān, a plural of abundance; both forms can serve as either plural and refer to the same number.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وخلف { لفتيانه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatā means a young man and fatāh a young woman; fatā is also a polite term for a servant, since young people and enslaved people commonly served.
rows.anchor: ويطلق على الخادم تلطفا ، لأنهم كانوا يستخفون بالشباب في الخدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍāʿa is money or goods prepared for trade; here it means the dirhams they paid for the food, as in the Torah.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها هنا الدراهم التي ابتاعوا بها الطعام كما في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph hoped they would recognize their own money by its local coinage or familiar purse and understand that Egypt’s ruler had deliberately returned it as a gift.
rows.anchor: رجاء أن يعرفوا أنها عين بضاعتهم إما بكونها مسكوك سكة بلادهم

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah’s account mentions recognition through the familiar bundles in which the money had been wrapped.
rows.anchor: وإما بمعرفة الصرر التي كانت مصرورة فيها كما في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riḥāl is the plural of raḥl, the rider’s baggage placed on a camel; the camel is consequently called rāḥila.
rows.anchor: والرحال : جمع رحل ، وهو ما يوضع على البعير من متاع الراكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inqilāb means returning, as in the Qur’anic reference to turning back on one’s heels.
rows.anchor: والانقلاب : الرجوع ، وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { انقلبتم على أعقابكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Perhaps they will return” answers Joseph’s command: seeing signs of their hardship, he feared they might lack money to buy provisions.
rows.anchor: وجملة لعلهم يرجعون } جواب للأمر في قوله : { اجعلوا بضاعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We have been denied measure” refers to future access: they already returned with food, and the construction presents measuring as something now withheld from them.
rows.anchor: معنى { منع منا الكيل } حيل بيننا وبين الكيل في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayl can denote active or passive measuring; here it is active, “we will measure.” Since they lacked goods to exchange, it means their request for provisions was refused unless their brother came.
rows.anchor: والكيل مصدر صالح لمعنى الفاعلية والمفعولية ، وهو هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an compresses their full account to Jacob: they may request provisions only if their brother accompanies them.
rows.anchor: فتعين أنه حكوا القصة لأبيهم مفصلة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read naktal with first-person plural, “we will measure.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { نكتل } بنون المتكلم المشارك

rows.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read yaktal, referring to their brother measuring with them.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف بتحتية عوض النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that they will protect their brother is conjoined to the request and emphatic through a nominal clause and “inna.”
rows.anchor: وأكدوا حفظه بالجملة الإسمية الدالة على الثبات وبحرف التوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s reply can mean either “I trust you as I trusted his brother” or “what good did trusting you with his brother do?”
rows.anchor: وجواب أبيهم كلام موجه يحتمل أن يكون معناه : { إني آمنكم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question challenges what their earlier pledge accomplished; his conclusion is that God is a better protector than they are.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام إنكاري فيه معنى النفي ، فهو يستفهم عن وجه التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God protects Benjamin, he will be safe; if not, he will not be safe, just as the brother entrusted to them before was lost.
rows.anchor: فإن حفظه الله سلم وإن لم يحفظه لم يسلم كما لم يسلم أخوه من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ originally means useful goods such as wares and clothes; here it denotes arranging and loading those goods, naming the action by its contents.
rows.anchor: وأطلق هنا على إعدال المتاع وإحماله من تسمية الشيء باسم الحال فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their address to their father begins a new explanatory clause because the audience awaits their reaction to the surprising discovery.
rows.anchor: وجملة قالوا يا أبانا } مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What more could we want?” may be an incredulous question or a negation; both mean they have no further request.
rows.anchor: و { ما } في قوله : { ما نبغي } يجوز أن يكون للاستفهام الإنكاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They knew the money was returned because it was found in the baggage after the food was packed, or because Joseph’s kindness and promise suggested it.
rows.anchor: وإنما علموا أنها ردت إليهم بقرينة وضعها في العدل بعد وضع الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We will provision our family” means that the returned money can buy the food they need to take home.
rows.anchor: وجملة ونمير أهلنا } معطوفة على جملة { هذه بضاعتنا ردت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mīra, with kasra on the mīm, means food brought from elsewhere.
rows.anchor: والميرة بكسر الميم بعدها ياء ساكنة : هي الطعام المجلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise to protect their brother follows naturally from travelling to fetch provisions and reassures Jacob, who had been asked to let him travel with them.
rows.anchor: وكانوا سألوا أباهم أن يكون أخوهم رفيقا لهم في الارتحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added camel-load gives Jacob another reason to send the brother: Joseph allotted one camel’s load per visitor, so the brother’s presence earns one more.
rows.anchor: لأن يوسف عليه السلام لا يعطي الممتار أكثر من حمل بعير من الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successive clauses are arranged elegantly, each developing from the previous one.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجمل مرتبة ترتيبا بديعا لأن بعضها متولد عن بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is an easy measure” points to the food already in their baggage; the measure noun stands for the measured object.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في { ذلك كيل يسير } إلى الطعام الذي في متاعهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says Jacob told them that the Egyptians may have forgotten the money, so they should disclose finding it when they return.
rows.anchor: قيل : إن يعقوب عليه السلام قال لهم : لعلهم نسوا البضاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People commonly say they “give” an oath when swearing to reassure the person receiving it; the opposite expression is to “take” an oath.
rows.anchor: اشتهر الإيتاء والإعطاء وما يراد بهما في إنشاء الحلف

rows.speaker: حديث الحشر
rows.claim: A report about the Gathering describes God giving pledges that He will not be asked for anything else, illustrating the oath idiom.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث الحشر ( فيعطي الله من عهود ومواثيق أن لا يسأله غيره )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an also speaks of “taking” a covenant, including Jacob’s pledge about Benjamin.
rows.anchor: كما أطلق فعل الأخذ على تلقي المحلوف له للحلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may be called given because ancient swearers handed over a token such as a whip or ring, or deposited collateral; the oath was understood as a surety.
rows.anchor: ولعل سبب إطلاق فعل الإعطاء أن الحالف كان في العصور القديمة يعطي المحلوف له شيئا تذكرة لليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mūthiq is originally a verbal noun of seeking assurance, used here for the pledge itself.
rows.anchor: والموثق : أصله مصدر ميمي للتوثق ، أطلق هنا على المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From God” modifies pledge: they are to call God as witness through an oath, making the covenant seem entrusted to God on the other party’s behalf.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ذلك أن يجعلوا الله شاهدا عليهم فيما وعدوا به بأن يحلفوا بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You will bring him” answers an implicit oath; the narrative adapts the sons’ wording to Jacob’s perspective, as in the reported speech of Jesus.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لتأتنني به } جواب لقسم محذوف دل عليه { موثقا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s second speech is narrated separately to mark a later moment: after accepting the pledge, he now gives advice as they prepare to depart.
rows.anchor: وإعادة فعل { قال } للإشارة إلى اختلاف زمن القولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells them to use separate city gates so their conspicuous foreign group will not arouse suspicion of espionage or theft and delay their arrival.
rows.anchor: خشية أن يسترعي عددهم أبصار أهل المدينة وحراسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is identified as Memphis, one of the world’s great cities with many gates; guards and watchers were stationed at its gates.
rows.anchor: وكانت مدينة ( منفيس ) من أعظم مدن العالم فهي ذات أبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proverb advises secrecy as a way to achieve one’s needs.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل في الحكمة : ( استعينوا على قضاء حوائجكم بالكتمان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob names separate gates to hide that the brothers form one group; he does not warn them about streets because they know the city, and Benjamin would travel with a brother.
rows.anchor: ووجه العدول عن المتعددة إلى المتفرقة الإيماء إلى علة الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His statement that he cannot avail them is parenthetical: his advice is only proper conduct and obedience, not protection from God’s decree.
rows.anchor: وما أغني عنكم بوصيتي هذه شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their precautions align with what God decrees, they gain both safety and obedience; otherwise they still gain the benefit of obeying and avoiding negligence.
rows.anchor: فإن صادف ما قدره فقد حصل فائدتان ، وإن خالف ما قدره حصلت فائدة امتثال أوامره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this usage aghnā is intransitive, meaning to suffice or serve as a substitute; the poet ʿAmr b. Maʿdīkarib’s line illustrates “suffice as a replacement.”
rows.anchor: ولذلك فمعنى فعل ( أغنى ) بهذا الاستعمال معنى الأفعال القاصرة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معديكرب
rows.claim: The cited line by ʿAmr b. Maʿdīkarib uses aghnā to illustrate the verb’s intransitive sense.
rows.anchor: كقول عمرو بن معديكرب : أغني غناء الذاهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the construction aghnā ʿan, ʿan marks substitution: Jacob cannot replace their own effort or suffice on their behalf.
rows.anchor: فمعنى ما أغني عنكم } لا أجزي عنكم ، أي لا أكفي بدلا عن إجزائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra min before “anything” strengthens the absolute negation; compare the verse denying that intercessors avail anything.
rows.anchor: و { من شيء } نائب مناب شيئا ، وزيدت { من } لتوكيد عموم شيء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats “anything” as an absolute object meaning even a little benefit, while also allowing a direct-object reading that requires an omitted preposition.
rows.anchor: وجوز صاحب الكشاف في مثله أن يكون شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Judgment belongs only to God” means that control and decree are God’s alone; nothing occurs except what He wills.
rows.anchor: والحكم : هنا بمعنى التصرف والتقدير ، ومعنى الحصر أنه لا يتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot resist God’s decree, but must pursue ordinary causes because God commands them to; the verse joins both duties.
rows.anchor: وليس للعبد أن ينازع مراد الله في نفس الأمر ولكن واجبه أن يتطلب الأمور من أسبابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob explains that taking precautions while relying on God is the proper meaning of trust, correcting people who either reduce or reject that balance.
rows.anchor: ليبين لهم أن وصيته بأخذ الأسباب مع التنبيه على الاعتماد على الله هو معنى التوكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to trust God applies to everyone, present and absent, and every believer of complete faith, not only the most righteous.
rows.anchor: وأن مقامه لا يختص بالصديقين بل هو واجب كل مؤمن كامل الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is parenthetical, introduced by an interjectory wāw.
rows.anchor: جملة معترضة ، والواو اعتراضية .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaythu indicates direction here; its clause identifies the direction from which they entered.
rows.anchor: ودلت { حيث } على الجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise narrative implies their travel, entry by the prescribed routes, and safe passage; those routes could not avert a divinely decreed calamity.
rows.anchor: وقد أغنت جملة { ولما دخلوا من حيث أمرهم أبوهم } عن جمل كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected because Jacob’s concern is not part of the negated protection; the sense is “but he fulfilled a concern in his mind.”
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا حاجة } منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaḍāhā means Jacob carried out his concern: he advised his sons so he could be sure he had not withheld useful guidance.
rows.anchor: والقضاء : الإنفاذ ، ومعنى قضاها أنفذها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concern was to warn them about dangers in travelling together and teach them both practical precautions and reliance on God.
rows.anchor: والحاجة التي في نفس يعقوب عليه السلام هي حرصه على تنبيههم للأخطار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement praises Jacob’s knowledge and wise management as knowledge taught to him by God, including prophetic knowledge.
rows.anchor: وهو ثناء على يعقوب عليه السلام بالعلم والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people fail to recognize both that precautions do not defeat God’s decree and that God commands ordinary means; they neglect one truth or the other.
rows.anchor: فإن مراد الله تعالى خفي عن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit praise for Jacob’s God-given knowledge and implicit contrast with most people praise him twice for observing both truths.
rows.anchor: ليتقرر الثناء على يعقوب عليه السلام باستفادته من الكلام مرتين

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: During the plague at ʿAmwās, Abū ʿUbayda asked whether Muslims were fleeing God’s decree; ʿUmar replied that they were moving from one decree to another.
rows.anchor: يا أبا عبيدة ألسنا نفر من قدر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative placement of Joseph’s arrival parallels the earlier account of the brothers’ entry, with omitted events understood.
rows.anchor: موقع جملة { ولما دخلوا على يوسف } كموقع جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āwā means bringing someone back to a dwelling; here it metaphorically means drawing Benjamin close so Joseph can whisper to him.
rows.anchor: وأطلق الإيواء هنا مجازا على الإدناء والتقريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s brief disclosure is rhetorically strong: emphatic inna, a nominal clause, and a separating pronoun assert that he alone is Benjamin’s brother, not a stranger.
rows.anchor: فأكد الخبر ب ( إن ) وبالجملة الإسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction reverses Benjamin’s assumption that Joseph was unrelated to him.
rows.anchor: فهو قصر قلب لاعتقاده أن الذي كلمه لا قرابة بينه وبينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to grieve refers to past mistreatment by the brothers, especially Benjamin’s sorrow over his presumed-dead full brother and their harshness and jealousy.
rows.anchor: وأراد بذلك ما كان يجده أخوه ( بنيامين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtāʾis means becoming sorrowful or distressed; the prohibition urges Benjamin to put grief aside and replace it with joy.
rows.anchor: والابتئاس : مطاوعة الإبئاس ، أي جعل أحد بائسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past form of “they were” points to prior deeds, while the imperfect “they did” suggests repeated harm and prepares Benjamin for the cup episode.
rows.anchor: وأفاد صوغ { يعملون } بصيغة المضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attribution that Joseph placed the cup is figurative causation: he ordered his servants to put it in the baggage.
rows.anchor: وإسناد جعل السقاية إلى ضمير يوسف مجاز عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The siqāya was a large vessel for water or wine; ṣuwāʿ is another name for a ṣāʿ measure, estimated at roughly a rattle and a quarter or a third.
rows.anchor: والسقاية : إناء كبير يسقى به الماء والخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine was customarily served by measured amounts according to each drinker’s tolerance, explaining why the vessel was called both a watering cup and a measure.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يشربون الخمر بالمقدار

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah calls the vessel a silver cup.
rows.anchor: وفي التوراة سمي طاسا ، ووصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in “the cup” refers to a vessel mentally understood as a normal fixture of a dignitary’s court.
rows.anchor: وتعريف { السقاية } تعريف العهد الذهني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it the king’s cup honors it and magnifies the theft, since state affairs belong to the king; alternatively, “king” may honor Joseph himself.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الصواع إلى الملك لتشريفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾdhīn is a repeated or emphatic call, as in the Qur’anic reference to a caller between the parties.
rows.anchor: والتأذين : النداء المكرر . وتقدم عند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĪr denotes the entire convoy: its camels or donkeys, loads, and riders.
rows.anchor: والعير : اسم للحمولة من إبل وحمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole convoy is accused by customary collective attribution of an offense committed by one member.
rows.anchor: وأسندت السرقة إلى جميعهم جريا على المعتاد من مؤاخذة الجماعة بجرم الواحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine demonstrative is used because ʿīr is understood as a group, with the riders as its salient members.
rows.anchor: وتأنيث اسم الإشارة وهو أيتها } لتأويل العير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ reply is a separate conversational answer to the herald’s call.
rows.anchor: وجملة { قالوا } جواب لنداء المنادي إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “they” who answer are the convoy; “they turned toward them” is circumstantial, with Joseph’s servants approaching the brothers.
rows.anchor: وضمير { قالوا } عائد إلى العير . وجملة { وأقبلوا عليهم } حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One of the approaching servants, their leader, guarantees the reward; zaʿīm means guarantor.
rows.anchor: والذي قال : { وأنا به زعيم } واحد من المقبلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although jurists cite this passage for reward contracts and guarantees, the author calls the proof weak: Joseph’s authority to legislate for Egypt, his prophethood, and followers there are unestablished.
rows.anchor: وفيه نظر ، لأن يوسف عليه السلام لم يكن يومئذ ذا شرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in “by God” is, in the preferred analysis, an oath particle used with God or Lord and for an extraordinary matter.
rows.anchor: والتاء في { تالله } حرف قسم على المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers swear because an earlier espionage suspicion was disproved when they truthfully described their father and brother; “the land” means Egypt.
rows.anchor: واتهموا بالجوسسة فتبينت براءتهم بما صدقوا يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also deny theft, perhaps because their money had accidentally been returned to their baggage.
rows.anchor: ولعلها وقعت في رحالهم غلطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of being thieves is stronger than denying an intent to corrupt: theft is a disgraceful trait, while espionage against an enemy may not be shameful to the accused.
rows.anchor: نفوا عن أنفسهم الاتصاف بالسرقة بأبلغ مما نفوا به الإفساد عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants make the brothers adjudicate the alleged offense by asking them to name its penalty.
rows.anchor: وقول الفتيان { فما جزاؤه إن كنتم كاذبين } تحكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What is its recompense?” means “what is its punishment?”; the pronoun refers to the cup by implication of its thief or theft, and lying means the cup is found in their bags.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { ما جزاؤه } : ما عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about whoever has the cup in his baggage can parse with man as conditional or relative; either way, that person himself becomes the penalty, meaning he remains with the cup’s owner rather than being killed.
rows.anchor: و { من } يجوز أن تكون شرطية وهي مبتدأ ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their repeated statement confirms the ruling, and the brothers’ own agreement binds them to it.
rows.anchor: فتكون جملة { فهو جزاؤه } توكيدا لفظيا لجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph ordered the search to begin with the other brothers’ containers before Benjamin’s.
rows.anchor: { بدأ } أي أمر يوسف عليه السلام بالبداءة بأوعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with the others’ bags prevented the search from appearing aimed at Benjamin from the outset; the feminine pronoun refers to the cup.
rows.anchor: والابتداء بأوعية غير أخيه لإبعاد أن يكون الذي يوجد في وعائه هو المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using a feminine pronoun for the siqāya is rhetorically apt because the object was a watering vessel shaped as a measuring cup, a return of ending to beginning.
rows.anchor: وهذا التأنيث في تمام الرشاقة إذ كانت الحقيقة أنها سقاية جعلت صواعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of “Thus We planned for Joseph” parallels the explanation of “Thus We requite wrongdoers.”
rows.anchor: والقول في { كذلك كدنا ليوسف } كالقول في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s plan was inspiring Joseph with the precise stratagem of placing and searching for the cup, and inspiring the brothers to stipulate the penalty; God is its cause and Joseph its beneficiary.
rows.anchor: والكيد : هنا هو إلهام يوسف عليه السلام لهذه الحيلة المحكمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view says Egyptian law punished theft by taking the item, beating the thief, and imposing twice its value.
rows.anchor: فقد قيل : إن شرعهم في جزاء السارق أن يؤخذ منه الشيء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains “in the king’s law” as his judgment, under which thieves were enslaved.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد { في دين الملك } أي حكمه وهو استرقاق السراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers Mujāhid’s sense of law or religious code: the verse indicates Egypt’s just king would not seize anyone without right; enslavement for theft was known among nations.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي يقتضيه ظاهر الآية لقوله : { ما كان ليأخذ أخاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of denial negates any ordinary cause that would authorize Joseph to keep Benjamin.
rows.anchor: ومعنى لام الجحود هنا نفي أن يكون في نفس الأمر سبب يخول يوسف عليه السلام أخذ أخيه عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception covers all otherwise-denied grounds for taking him; an omitted causal bi means “except by God’s willing,” inspiring and permitting the act for broad future benefit.
rows.anchor: فالتقدير : إلا بأن يشاء الله ، أي يلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raising of ranks summarizes the episode: Joseph rises through wise management, Benjamin through joining him and learning, and their family later through Joseph’s compassion.
rows.anchor: فيها رفع درجة يوسف عليه السلام في الحال بالتدبير الحكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Degrees metaphorically represent honor, as in Qur’anic references to rank between men and ranks with God.
rows.anchor: فالدرجات مستعارة لقوة الشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing” generalizes degrees of created knowledge and points to God’s unlimited knowledge; above is metaphorical for superiority.
rows.anchor: وفيها شاهد لتفاوت الناس في العلم المؤذن بأن علم الذي خلق لهم العلم لا ينحصر مداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal reading must exclude God from having anyone above Him, as reason establishes.
rows.anchor: ويتعين تخصيص هذا العموم بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى بدليل العقل إذ ليس فوق الله عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite “one more knowing” can denote one exalted individual—God—so the wording needs no restriction.
rows.anchor: وقد يحمل التنكير على الوحدة ويكون المراد عليم واحد فيكون التنكير للوحدة والتعظيم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read “degrees of whomever We will” with iḍāfa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { درجات من نشاء } بإضافة { درجات }

rows.speaker: حمزة، عاصم، الكسائي، وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamza, ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read tanwīn on darajāt, treating it as a specification attached to the verb’s object.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة ، وعاصم ، والكسائي ، وخلف بتنوين { درجات }

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي وأبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and Abū Ḥayyān take the pronoun in “he concealed it” to mean the brothers’ accusation: Joseph bore the insult without showing anger, rebuking, or punishing them.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا التفسير ينحو أبو علي الفارسي وأبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, “You are worse in state” is a separate reply: their theft is witnessed, while their charge against Benjamin is only an allegation.
rows.anchor: أي أنتم أشد شرا في حالتكم هذه لأن سرقتكم مشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “he said” favors taking Joseph’s “you are worse” as a new utterance rather than part of the concealed speech.
rows.anchor: وفعل { قال } يرجح هذا الوجه

rows.speaker: الزجاج والزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj and al-Zamakhsharī take the pronoun to anticipate Joseph’s following statement, as a feminine pronoun of the affair or utterance that the next clause explains.
rows.anchor: وبهذا فسر الزجاج والزمخشري ، أي قال في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second interpretation, concealment is literal: Joseph hid the words from anyone who might hear them.
rows.anchor: والإسرار ، على هذا الوجه ، مستعمل في حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He did not disclose it to them” may reinforce concealment, with “to them” implying he told Benjamin they lied; alternatively, it means he showed them neither anger nor punishment.
rows.anchor: قيل هي توكيد لجملة { فأسرها يوسف }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shar is the comparative of ashar; makānan is a specification, and “place” metaphorically means their state.
rows.anchor: و { شر } اسم تفضيل ، وأصله أشر ، و { مكانا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ logic would make them even more likely thieves because they had two allegedly thieving brothers; alternatively, they are worse because they falsely accused innocent brothers and threw Joseph into the well.
rows.anchor: والكلام قابل للحمل على معنى أنتم شر حالة من أخيكم هذا والذي قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Joseph al-ʿAzīz because a ruler over an important office bore that title, as did the chief of police; alternatively, Joseph inherited the purchaser’s authority over several functions.
rows.anchor: نادوا بوصف العزيز إما لأن كل رئيس ولاية مهمة يدعى بما يرادف العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They describe their father through paternal affection, old age, and standing as clan elder or extreme age to move Joseph’s compassion; these facts were already known to him.
rows.anchor: ووصفوا أباهم بثلاث صفات تقتضي الترقيق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father’s being “great” may mean leader of his clan or an intensifier of his old age; this explains their offer to substitute an older brother for Benjamin, the youngest.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكبير : إما كبير عشيرته فإساءته تسوءهم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We see you as one of the beneficent” motivates compliance rather than the request itself: a generous person will not distress an old father.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إنا نراك من المحسنين } تعليل لإجابة المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makān is literally where a body settles, but here metaphorically means a substitute occupying the place of the person exchanged, as in a hadith about substitute pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: والمكان : أصله محل الكون أي ما يستقر فيه الجسم ، وهو هنا مجاز في العوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿādh is a verbal noun meaning refuge; with its governing verb omitted it means “I seek refuge in God” from taking anyone except the person whose baggage held the cup.
rows.anchor: و { معاذ } مصدر ميمي اسم للعوذ ، وهو اللجأ إلى مكان للتحصن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the person whom the brothers themselves designated as penalty is legitimate under their agreed ruling; taking another would be unjust.
rows.anchor: لأن أخذ من وجد المتاع عنده صار حقا عليه بحكمه على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s plural “we” may be a majestic plural used by a ruler, or a humble inclusive form; compare the statement attributed to Khiḍr.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون من استعمال ضمير الجمع في التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph may have concealed his identity because his brothers might harm Benjamin on the way home, or bringing Jacob’s clan to Egypt amid political hostility might arouse suspicion; he may have waited for a safer opportunity or wanted to learn the family’s situation from Benjamin.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يكاشفهم يوسف عليه السلام بحاله ويأمرهم بجلب أبيهم يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istayʾasū means they despaired; the extra sīn and tāʾ intensify the meaning, as in the cited forms “He answered him” and “he resisted.”
rows.anchor: { استيأسوا } بمعنى يئسوا فالسين والتاء للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their despair “of him” concerns Joseph’s releasing their brother; using the person’s name intensifies reference to the relevant state.
rows.anchor: واليأس منه : اليأس من إطلاقه أخاهم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read istayʾasū with the standard yāʾ and hamza sequence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { استيأسوا } بتحتية بعد الفوقية

rows.speaker: البزي عن ابن كثير
rows.claim: Al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr has a variant with an alif after the tāʾ, treating it as metathesis followed by replacement of the hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأه البزي عن ابن كثير بخلف عنه بألف بعد الفوقية ثم تحتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaṣū means they separated and became alone; its root denotes purity from mixture.
rows.anchor: و { خلصوا } بمعنى اعتزلوا وانفردوا

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
rows.claim: At ʿUmar’s final pilgrimage, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf advised postponing a speech about a faction seeking the caliphate until Medina, where ʿUmar could speak privately with learned people.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول عبد الرحمن بن عوف لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنهما في آخر حجة حجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najī is a verbal noun used adjectivally in the singular masculine; it means the brothers withdrew to speak privately, as in “when they were in private counsel.”
rows.anchor: والنجي : اسم من المناجاة ، وانتصابه على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their eldest said” is an appositional expansion of their private counsel; the eldest is Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.
rows.anchor: وكبيرهم هو أكبرهم سنا وهو روبين بكر يعقوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “Do you not know?” is a reminder that Jacob no longer trusts their protection of his son.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام في { ألم تعلموا } تقريري مستعمل في التذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical phrase means their failure with Joseph preceded this pledge, so their father will not believe their explanation of Benjamin’s theft; the eldest stays as proof of their sincerity.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ومن قبل ما فرطتم } جملة معترضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Or God decides for me” contrasts the plan the eldest set for himself with whatever God decrees beyond his power; the verb’s complement is omitted.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { أو يحكم الله لي } ترديد بين ما رسمه هو لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām marks purpose: God may decree what benefits him, with “judging” meaning determining.
rows.anchor: واللام للأجل ، أي يحكم الله بما فيه نفعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He is the best of judges” either means God’s judgment is never unjust or cannot be overturned; contextually it also praises God while indirectly asking for relief and return from exile.
rows.anchor: و { خير الحاكمين } إن كان على التعميم فهو الذي حكمه لا جور فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Benjamin’s failure to defend himself suggests he stayed silent because he knew Joseph intended to keep him, as Joseph had privately disclosed earlier.
rows.anchor: يدل على أنه لازم السكوت لأنه كان مطلعا على مراد يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eldest coaches his brothers on what to tell Jacob; “we were not guardians of the unseen” means they could not know hidden facts, either to soften the accusation or because they doubted Benjamin had stolen.
rows.anchor: احتراس من تحقق كونه سرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We were not guardians of the unseen” uses preservation to mean knowledge of hidden circumstances.
rows.anchor: والغيب : الأحوال الغائبة عن المرء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking the village means asking its inhabitants; the city is Egypt, and city and village are near synonyms, though “city” conventionally means the larger settlement.
rows.anchor: وسؤال القرية مجاز عن سؤال أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan means their travelling companions from Canaan; they can ask the caravan easily and verify the city’s account by sending, corresponding, or travelling there.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعير التي كانوا فيها رفاقهم في عيرهم القادمين إلى مصر
